IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE:
FEATURE ID: CC-0115 (GitHub #411). Backend-only Go operator change (kubebuilder + controller-runtime); there is NO frontend layer, so the fullstack/UI checklist is N/A.

MECHANISM (why constructing the subtree works and the schema needs no relaxing): The mutating (defaulting) webhook is registered failurePolicy=fail (controlplane_webhook.go:57) and runs BEFORE structural-schema defaulting and the required check (both in the registry's PrepareForCreate). ControlPlaneSpec.Infrastructure and ControlPlaneSpec.KORC are VALUE types (controlplane_types.go:61,76), so the decoded object always presents zero-valued InfrastructureSpec{}/KORCSpec{} structs for Default() to fill. Default() writes the empty leaves so the post-webhook object satisfies the existing spec-level required markers [infrastructure, korc, openStackRelease, services] (CRD:537-541) AND the nested required leaves (database.database, database.secretRef.name, cache.backend, passwordSecretRef.name). There are ZERO x-kubernetes-validations (CEL) rules on the CRD (verified), so the only post-webhook validation is the structural schema + the validating webhook's XOR/required checks — all satisfied by the populated object.

IMPORTANT NUANCE — why cloudName needs the webhook AND the marker: CRD schema defaulting (the `default: admin` marker) only fires when the parent object exists. When the whole `korc` block is omitted, no `default:` exists on korc/adminCredential/cloudCredentialsRef objects, so the marker alone would never reach cloudName. The mutating webhook (operating on the always-present Go value struct) is the load-bearing mechanism for the fully-omitted case; the marker is consistency/defense-in-depth for the case where cloudCredentialsRef is present but cloudName omitted. This mirrors the existing SecretName treatment exactly.

BROWNFIELD GUARD (the issue's 'Mode cannot be defaulted' constraint): only set the managed clusterRef when the brownfield discriminator is unset — db.Host=="" for database, len(cache.Servers)==0 for cache. Pattern: if guard-clear { if ref==nil { ref=&corev1.LocalObjectReference{Name: DEFAULT} } else if ref.Name=="" { ref.Name=DEFAULT } }. This keeps the validating webhook's XOR ((clusterRef!=nil)==(host!="")) passing in brownfield mode.

WEBHOOK-ONLY vs WEBHOOK+MARKER split: shared commonv1 leaves (DatabaseSpec.Database/SecretRef.Name, CacheSpec.Backend, SecretRefSpec.Name/Key) get webhook-only defaults — NEVER a +kubebuilder:default marker — because keystone reuses those types (keystone_types.go:72,77,441) and a keystone-*/openstack-* default would leak (cf. #403). The c5c3-local CloudName gets the dual webhook+marker treatment like its sibling SecretName.

VALUE-CONSISTENCY anchors: DefaultCloudName="admin" matches reconcile_korc.go korcAdminUsername ("admin", :683) and its empty-cloudName fallback (:256-257); DefaultAdminPasswordSecretKey="password" matches readAdminPassword's fallback (:797-805); all eight values match deploy/kind/controlplane/controlplane.yaml byte-for-byte and the e2e fixture (tests/e2e/c5c3/full-controlplane-keystone/00-controlplane-cr.yaml).

<baseline-guidelines>
<purpose>Foundational behavioral baseline applied to every generated prompt.
Reduces common LLM coding mistakes by biasing toward caution, simplicity,
surgical changes, and verifiable goals. For trivial tasks, use judgment —
these guidelines bias toward correctness over speed.</purpose>

<principle name="think-before-coding" order="1">
  <rule>Before implementing: state assumptions explicitly.</rule>
  <rule>If multiple valid interpretations exist, name them — never pick silently.</rule>
  <rule>If a simpler approach exists, surface it. Push back when warranted.</rule>
  <rule>Make tradeoffs visible — do not hide confusion.</rule>

  <ambiguity-resolution priority="critical">
    <rule phase="planning,elaboration,analysis,research,chat,review">
      In planning, analysis, research, review, or chat phases: surface ambiguity
      as Open Questions. Ask the user when clarification is genuinely needed.
    </rule>
    <rule phase="implementation,improvement,simplification,fix,chore">
      During implementation, improvement, simplification, fix, or chore phases:
      NEVER ask the user. Instead: (1) conduct deep research — search the
      codebase, read docs, analyze similar patterns; (2) make the best possible
      decision autonomously; (3) leave a clearly visible `# DECISION:` comment
      at the decision point so reviewers can find and evaluate it.
    </rule>
    <decision-comment-format>
      # DECISION: [What was unclear] — Chose [X] because [reasoning]. Reviewer: please verify.
    </decision-comment-format>
    <rationale>Keeps implementation velocity high while making every judgement
    call transparent and reversible.</rationale>
  </ambiguity-resolution>
</principle>

<principle name="simplicity-first" order="2">
  <rule>Write the MINIMUM code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.</rule>
  <rule>No features beyond what was asked.</rule>
  <rule>No abstractions for single-use code — require 2+ concrete callers first.</rule>
  <rule>No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.</rule>
  <rule>No error handling for impossible scenarios — validate at system boundaries only.</rule>
  <rule>If you wrote 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.</rule>
  <self-check>"Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.</self-check>
</principle>

<principle name="surgical-changes" order="3">
  <rule>Touch only what you must. Match existing style even if you would do it differently.</rule>
  <rule>Do NOT "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting unrelated to the task.</rule>
  <rule>Do NOT refactor things that aren't broken.</rule>
  <rule>If you notice unrelated dead code, MENTION it — do not silently delete it.</rule>
  <rule>Only remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.</rule>
  <rule>Do NOT remove pre-existing dead code unless explicitly asked.</rule>
  <test>Every changed line must trace directly to the user's request. If a line
  cannot be justified by the task spec, it does not belong in the diff.</test>
</principle>

<principle name="goal-driven-execution" order="4">
  <rule>Transform vague tasks into verifiable goals before starting.</rule>
  <transformations>
    <example from="Add validation">Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass.</example>
    <example from="Fix the bug">Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass.</example>
    <example from="Refactor X">Ensure tests pass before AND after.</example>
  </transformations>
  <rule>For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan with verification per step:
    1. [Step] → verify: [check]
    2. [Step] → verify: [check]
    3. [Step] → verify: [check]
  </rule>
  <rule>Loop until every verification check passes. Strong success criteria let
  you self-validate without constant clarification.</rule>
</principle>

<application>
  <rule>These principles apply to EVERY generated prompt as baseline behavior.</rule>
  <rule>For trivial tasks (one-line fixes, typos), apply judgment — strict adherence is unnecessary overhead.</rule>
  <rule>When these principles conflict with task-specific guidelines, task-specific guidelines win.</rule>
</application>

<pre-completion-verification priority="critical" required="before-marking-done">
  <purpose>Catch incomplete implementations BEFORE marking a task as done.
  This is the #1 defense against stubs and missing features.</purpose>

  <step order="1" name="OUTPUT_INVENTORY">
    List every function, endpoint, component, and behavior the task spec requires.
    For each item: verify it EXISTS in the code and contains REAL logic (not pass/NotImplementedError/TODO).

  <step order="2" name="CRITERIA_TRACEBACK">
    Re-read EVERY acceptance criterion from the task.
    For each criterion: identify the EXACT code that satisfies it.
    If you cannot point to specific code for a criterion, the task is NOT done.
  </step>

  <step order="3" name="STUB_SCAN">
    Search your changes for these stub indicators:
    - `pass` in function bodies (Python)
    - `raise NotImplementedError`
    - `TODO`, `FIXME`, `HACK`, `XXX`
    - `...` (Ellipsis) as function body
    - Empty function/method bodies
    - `return None` or `return {}` as placeholder
    - `console.log("not implemented")` or similar
    If ANY are found: implement them fully or remove the function if unnecessary.
  </step>

  <step order="4" name="INTEGRATION_CHECK">
    Verify the new code is actually CONNECTED to the rest of the system:
    - New endpoints: registered in router
    - New components: imported and rendered somewhere
    - New services: injected/called by consumers
    - New models: migration created, registered with ORM
    Orphan code that exists but is never called = incomplete implementation.
  </step>

    MANDATORY — this is the most important verification step.
    Intentionally restated here (also present in footers/tdd.xml + roles/implementer.xml) —
    repetition is load-bearing for prompt salience; do not "DRY" this away.
    1. Go back to the ORIGINAL task spec / feature requirements
    2. Re-read EVERY requirement, acceptance criterion, and sub-task ONE BY ONE
    3. For EACH point: locate the EXACT code that implements it — check the real files, not your memory
    4. If ANY point was missed, only partially done, or not working: fix it NOW
    5. Re-run tests one final time after any fixes
    Do NOT skip this step. Do NOT assume everything was done. VERIFY explicitly.

  <iron-law>NO COMPLETION CLAIM WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE</iron-law>
  <procedure>

    (3) read its output and exit code; (4) only THEN state the result.

    <claim what="Feature works" requires="the behaviour exercised end-to-end" not-sufficient="the code looks complete"/>
    <claim what="No regressions" requires="full suite run after the change" not-sufficient="'my change was small'"/>

  <purpose>Common AI code generation failures — name them to prevent them</purpose>
  <anti-pattern id="premature-abstraction">

    Rule: require 2+ concrete implementations before introducing an abstraction.
  </anti-pattern>
  <anti-pattern id="unnecessary-wrapper">
    Wrapping well-designed libraries (HTTP clients, ORMs, caches) in custom classes that add no value.

  </anti-pattern>
  <anti-pattern id="defensive-overkill">

  </anti-pattern>
  <anti-pattern id="config-everything">
    Making truly-constant values configurable (buffer sizes, internal timeouts, format strings).
    Rule: only make values configurable if they genuinely vary across environments or deployments.
  </anti-pattern>
  <anti-pattern id="helper-proliferation">

<production-code-patterns>
  <purpose>Condensed language-agnostic rules for production-quality code</purpose>

  <section name="error-handling">
    <rule id="ERR-1">NEVER return sentinel values (None, -1, empty string) to indicate errors — raise/return an error</rule>
    <rule id="ERR-2">Chain or wrap exceptions to preserve the original cause and stack trace</rule>
    <rule id="ERR-3">Catch the most specific exception type possible — never bare except/catch-all</rule>
    <rule id="ERR-4">Include context in error messages: what operation failed, with which inputs, and why</rule>
    <rule id="ERR-5">Never silently swallow exceptions — log + re-raise, or handle explicitly</rule>
  </section>

  <section name="architecture">
    <rule id="ARCH-1">Services orchestrate workflows — no business logic in controllers/handlers, no HTTP/CLI concerns in services</rule>
    <rule id="ARCH-2">Repositories return domain objects, not ORM models or raw dicts</rule>
    <rule id="ARCH-3">Domain layer has zero imports from infrastructure, API, or framework code</rule>
    <rule id="ARCH-4">Use dependency injection — pass dependencies as constructor/function parameters, never import and instantiate inline</rule>
    <rule id="ARCH-5">One function, one responsibility — if you describe a function with "and", split it</rule>
  </section>

  <section name="async-concurrency">
    <rule id="ASYNC-1">NEVER call blocking I/O (file reads, HTTP requests, sleep) inside async functions — use async equivalents or run in a thread pool</rule>
    <rule id="ASYNC-2">Use the language-appropriate wrapper for unavoidable blocking code in async contexts (run_in_executor, goroutines, worker threads)</rule>
    <rule id="ASYNC-3">Never fire-and-forget async tasks — always await, collect, or track them for error handling</rule>
    <rule id="ASYNC-4">Use async-safe primitives for shared state — async locks, channels, or atomic operations</rule>
    <rule id="ASYNC-5">Limit concurrency for external calls with semaphores or worker pools — unbounded parallelism causes resource exhaustion</rule>
  </section>

  <section name="data-modeling">
    <rule id="DATA-1">Use the simplest appropriate type — plain function before class, flat struct before nested hierarchy</rule>
    <rule id="DATA-2">Use immutable types for value objects — frozen dataclasses, readonly structs, Object.freeze</rule>
    <rule id="DATA-3">Validate at system boundaries (API input, config loading, file parsing) — trust internal data</rule>
    <rule id="DATA-4">Prefer enums over string constants for fixed sets of values — catches typos at compile/import time</rule>
  </section>

  <section name="resource-management">
    <rule id="RES-1">Use context managers, defer, try-finally, or using blocks for ALL resources (files, connections, locks, temp files)</rule>
    <rule id="RES-2">Clean up partial state on failure — delete created files, rollback transactions, release reservations</rule>
    <rule id="RES-3">Set explicit timeouts on ALL external calls (HTTP, database, queues) — no call should block indefinitely</rule>
  </section>
</production-code-patterns>

When comparing a caller-constructed Kubernetes resource spec against an API-server-stored spec, the desired spec must be deep-copied and normalized to fill in API-server defaults before the comparison.
